identity.title: NeuroClips: Towards High-fidelity and Smooth fMRI-to-Video Reconstruction

problem.claim: Reconstruct continuous video stimuli from non-invasive fMRI while preserving semantic content, perceptual detail, fidelity, and temporal smoothness.

gap.claim: Compared with static visual reconstruction, fMRI-to-video research remains limited because decoding spatiotemporal perception from continuous experiences is highly challenging.

contributions.claim: NeuroClips combines a semantics reconstructor for video keyframes with a perception reconstructor for low-level perceptual details and flows.
The framework injects reconstructed keyframes and low-level perception flows into a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion model during inference.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present NeuroClips as an innovative framework targeting high-fidelity and smooth video reconstruction from fMRI by jointly decoding semantic and low-level perceptual information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report reconstruction of videos up to 6 seconds at 8 FPS on a publicly available fMRI-video dataset.

The authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art models across various metrics on a publicly available fMRI-video dataset, including a 128% improvement in SSIM and an 81% improvement in unspecified spatiotemporal metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Static visual reconstruction from fMRI has achieved substantial progress with deep learning models such as CLIP and Stable Diffusion.
Video reconstruction remains limited because continuous visual experiences require decoding spatiotemporal perception.
The authors argue that both high-level semantics and low-level perceptual flows must be decoded accurately.
NeuroClips reconstructs semantic keyframes and perceptual details, then conditions a pre-trained T2V diffusion model with both signals.
On a public dataset, the authors report smooth, high-fidelity reconstruction up to 6 seconds at 8 FPS and gains over existing models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates semantic reconstruction of keyframes from low-level perception-flow reconstruction, assigning each to a stated target: semantic accuracy and consistency versus smoothness.

lessons.interpretation: Decomposing a difficult generation objective into components aligned with distinct perceptual properties can make the design rationale more traceable.
lessons.application: For another multimodal reconstruction task, define separate intermediate representations for content identity and temporal or perceptual continuity, and connect each explicitly to its intended evaluation dimension.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when the target properties cannot be represented independently or when separate modules introduce incompatible errors.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset size, stimulus composition, baselines, metric definitions, or statistical testing details.
The reported percentage improvements lack the underlying scores and comparison conditions.
